sections.h2: What kind of county is Jasper County, Georgia?
sections.html:
Jasper County is a rural, central Georgia county of about 373 square miles, with Monticello as its only city and seat and Shady Dale as its one town. The General Assembly formed it on December 10, 1807 from Baldwin County land, first under the name Randolph, and renamed it for Sergeant William Jasper in 1812, according to Wikipedia.

The county borders Morgan, Putnam, Jones, Monroe, Butts and Newton counties. Part of the Oconee National Forest and the Piedmont National Wildlife Refuge lie inside it, so a share of the land is public. West of a line that follows State Route 11, water runs to the Upper Ocmulgee River; the east side drains toward the Upper Oconee.

The 2020 count found every resident living in a rural area, with a median age of 41.7. The Jasper County School District has four schools, including Jasper County High School. The Jasper County courthouse appears in the 1992 film My Cousin Vinny.

sections.h2: How has Jasper County grown, and what does it mean for a home seller?
sections.html:
Growth has picked up after decades of decline. Census estimates put the county at 17,632 in July 2025, which is 20.8% above the April 2020 base of 14,599.

Jasper County's population was just 5,760 in 1970 and 11,426 in 2000. The 39.2-minute average commute is long, and the county belongs to the Atlanta-Sandy Springs-Roswell metro area. In 2020, 13.7% of the 6,270 housing units were vacant. With density at only 39.6 people per square mile, acreage sales are common and buyers often ask about wells, septic systems and road frontage.

sections.h2: Who handles what in Jasper County's tax system?
sections.html:
Each office has one job. The Tax Assessor values property, the Board of Equalization hears disputes, the Board of Commissioners and the Board of Education set millage, and the Tax Commissioner bills and collects.

  • Tax Commissioner: 126 W. Greene Street, Suite 125, Monticello, GA 31064; phone (706) 468-4902; Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Tax Assessor: approves exemptions, reviews appeals and mails notices when a value changes.
  • Board of Equalization: appointed by the Grand Jury and hears administrative appeals.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: deed room in the Jasper County Courthouse, where you can get a copy of a warranty deed.

One mill equals $1 for each $1,000 of assessed value, and assessed value is 40% of fair market value under O.C.G.A. 48-5-7. Tax Commissioner staff do not set either number.

sections.h2: When are Jasper County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The county's standing rule splits real estate and business personal property bills into two halves, due September 20 and December 20. The county's 2026 notice moved the first date: bills were mailed October 16, the first installment carried a November 20 date, and the balance carries December 20.

Because the first date has moved from year to year, read the dates printed on your bill. The same Tax Commissioner site says the schedule is "normally" September 20 and December 20.

  • Mobile and manufactured homes: April 1 each year, with the location permit issued at payment
  • Late mobile home payment: 10% penalty, a citation to Magistrate Court, or sale of the home
  • Motor vehicles: due by the owner's birthday

Updating your mailing address with the Tax Assessor or Tax Commissioner matters, since tax notices go to the last address on file.

sections.h2: What happens if a Jasper County bill goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid property can be levied upon and eventually sold, and a lien can reach your credit file well before that. When taxes stay unpaid more than 90 days after the due date, a tax FiFa (lien) is recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court.

Those records are public. Credit bureaus can read them, and the tax office says it has no control over how they use the information or how often they refresh it. A seller with a FiFa on record should plan to clear it before closing.

Call (706) 468-4902 for a payoff, then give that figure to whoever handles the closing. If the house changed hands midyear, ask who the office considers responsible for each installment, since the first and second halves can fall on opposite sides of the sale date.

sections.h2: Which Jasper County homestead exemptions are listed?
sections.html:
The county lists a $2,000 standard homestead exemption, deducted from the 40% assessed value. It covers the county, the school system and the State levy, but not the part of the rate that retires bond debt.

  • Elderly school tax (age 62 or older): up to $10,000 off assessed value when net income does not exceed $10,000; school tax only, bonds included
  • Elderly general (age 65 or older): up to $4,000 when net income of applicant and spouse does not exceed $10,000; Social Security and certain retirement income are excluded
  • Disabled veterans: up to $63,780 for qualifying service-connected disabilities, with a matching exemption for an unremarried surviving spouse of a service member killed in armed conflict
  • Age 65 and older, State levy: the full value of the home and up to 10 acres, for those who qualify for another homestead exemption

File at the Tax Commissioner's office and bring a driver's license showing your Jasper County address. The application must arrive by April 1 to count for that year, and an approved exemption renews on its own until your residence, ownership or exemption type changes. Where a local county exemption is larger than the State amount, the local one applies.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Jasper County assessment?
sections.html:
Appeal in writing within 45 days of the assessment notice date, either to the Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator. After that decision, you can carry the matter to Superior Court by filing a written notice with the Board of Tax Assessors.

You can also set the stage in advance. Between January 1 and April 1 any owner may file a return stating what they think the property was worth on January 1. If the assessors then raise the figure, that return establishes your right to appeal. Owners of mobile homes who disagree with the value have 45 days to file with the Board of Tax Assessors, then 21 days from a change notice to go to the Board of Equalization.

sections.h2: What returns, notices and special assessments apply in Jasper County?
sections.html:
Every property owner must return taxable property to the Tax Commissioner's office between January 1 and April 1. An owner who files nothing is treated as having returned the same property at the same value and with the same real property exemptions as the year before.

A return can also state your own opinion of fair market value as of January 1. If the assessors later change that figure, the return is what sets up your right to appeal. Jasper County sends tax notices to the last address on file, so report a new mailing address right away to either the Tax Assessor or the Tax Commissioner.

  • Historic property: a building listed on the Georgia register, plus up to two surrounding acres, may qualify for preferential assessment
  • Brownfield property: a site approved under the State's Hazardous Site Reuse and Redevelopment Program can have its value frozen for ten years
  • Surviving spouses: an unremarried surviving spouse of a firefighter or peace officer killed in duty can receive a total exemption, with agency documents

The Board of Tax Assessors explains the ownership and use rules for each program. If you plan to sell land or a building that is enrolled in one, ask what the new owner would have to do to keep the status.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Jasper County Tax Commissioner?
faqs.a: Call (706) 468-4902 or visit 126 W. Greene Street, Suite 125, in Monticello. The office is open Monday to Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for a Jasper County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: April 1 of the year you first claim it. An application received after that date applies to the next tax year, and you must own and live in the home on January 1.

faqs.q: Can a late Jasper County bill hurt my credit?
faqs.a: It can. After 90 days unpaid, a FiFa lien is recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court, and credit bureaus can read those public records.

faqs.q: Where do I get a copy of my Jasper County deed?
faqs.a: The Clerk of Superior Court's deed room in the Jasper County Courthouse can provide a copy of your warranty deed.

faqs.q: How long do I have to dispute a Jasper County value?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date on the assessment notice to appeal to the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator. A later step to Superior Court follows a written notice.
